learning: If slalom progress rises above 0.32 and max_error falls toward 0.06 m with oval and s-bend completion holding, the mismatch bias is still a live slalom limit and ki can go higher. If s-bend completion drops below 18 of 20 or oscillation rises sharply, the integral is overshooting, so return ki to 0.4 and test wheel_track of about 0.10 m next. If progress stays flat near 0.32, the integral is saturated and the reversal reaction is the limit.
notes: Geometry held at the iteration-7 values, as the Builder requested. Controller is the iteration-7 controller with ki raised from 0.4 to 0.7, so the integral term is the only change.
rationale:
Iteration 7 (ki 0.4, kd 0.8, kp 2.4, base 1.3, y = 0.07 m, 0.6 kg) is the best race so far at 673.6. Oval and s-bend both complete 20 of 20. The slalom still fails 0 of 20, with progress 0.3185, max_error 0.0632 m and 1.0 line-loss events per run. Iteration 4 showed that adding integral action (ki 0 to 0.2, with kd raised) lifted slalom progress from 0.198 to 0.278. The later step from ki 0.2 to 0.4 added only about 0.02 more progress, so the integral term is giving diminishing returns. Look-ahead is saturated (iteration 5), and line losses are well below the 2-per-run widening trigger, so the spread is not the limit.

The Builder held the iteration-7 geometry unchanged, so the controller is the only variable this iteration. I raise ki from 0.4 to 0.7 to test whether a stronger integral can remove more of the fixed motor-mismatch bias on the slalom. The integral is clamped to +/-2, so windup is bounded. kp 2.4, kd 0.8, base_speed 1.3 and last_direction line loss stay as before. I expect slalom progress to rise above 0.32 and oval and s-bend completion to hold. The main risk is overshoot after bends, which would show as lower s-bend completion or higher oscillation (s-bend oscillation is about 0.29 in iteration 7). This is a hypothesis, not a measured result.
